references.text: David asks that the Lord should destroy Joab's house because they have despised the word of the Lord; the same principle applies: despising God's word leads to judgment.
Nathan tells David that he has despised the word of the Lord through his sin; the same Hebrew expression 'בָּזָה' (despised) is used.
Isaiah warns of judgment upon those who reject the law of the Lord and despise the words of the Holy One.
The one who despises the word shall perish, while the one who fears the commandment will receive a reward.
The same principle applies: being cut off from the people for anyone who intentionally fails to keep the Passover.
Breaking the covenant leads to being cut off from the people; the same expression 'הִכָּרֵת' (shall be cut off) is used.
Whoever profanes the Sabbath shall be cut off from his people, facing the same judgment for breaking the Lord's command.
A warning about the consequences of despising the Lord's statutes and rejecting His laws.
The one who rejects the law of Moses shall die, and an even worse punishment awaits those who trample God's Son underfoot.
The house of Israel rebelled against the Lord and profaned their Sabbaths; they despised His statutes.
